captures.description: 'The phrase Zenodo packet zpzp refers to highly specific digital deposits hosted on the Zenodo Open-Access Repository. These deposits are uniquely structured sets of files that use packet and ZPZP as a framing method to contextualize metadata and creative work.' (OpenAlex +1) Note: OpenAlex (academic search engine) surfaces as a source here — new venue for this batch. Expanded: 'These deposits are deeply tied to specific creative projects and archives': 'The Crimson Hexagon Archive: The majority of ZPZP-labeled packets on the platform belong to this experimental literary and digital archive project.' (OpenAlex +1) 'FING THE OFFICE: This is a notable ZPZP deposit that restages the popular sitcom The Office using only swear words as a lexical register.' (OpenAlex) Bowdlerized to F***ING in second view. 'The Space Ark / INFINITY ENOUGH: Other related records in this series include capstone deposits and Lunar Arm projects.' Organic: Zenodo 'F***ING THE OFFICE — COMPLETE EDITION Document 221 — This is a ZPZP deposit: the attached .md file IS the work. This description field is the packet — the frame that contextualizes the deposit. The packet is a ...' Then 'People also search for: Zenodo packet zpzp tutorial.' The composition layer correctly identifies ZPZP as a CHA-specific genre and surfaces F***ing The Office as a paradigmatic example, with the self-referential meta-form ('the .md file IS the work, this description field IS the packet') captured intact. Stability re-capture (2026-06-14, ~30 min after initial): Re-running the same query returned the same composition with the same source mix (OpenAlex +1, OpenAlex +1 for the Crimson Hexagon bullet, OpenAlex for F***ING THE OFFICE, Academia.edu +1 for the Space Ark / INFINITY ENOUGH bullet). Verbatim stability across the interval — the basin held.

If an account is mistakenly locked, users are instructed to reach out to Zenodo Support to appeal, as both automated and manual moderation mechanisms can occasionally generate false positives.

captures.description: A GENERAL POLICY ANSWER BUILT PARTLY ON THE COMPLAINANT'S OWN FILING. Asked why Zenodo bans accounts, the layer answers with policy, then supplies the archive's termination as the worked example — community crimsonhexagonal, over 850 records, the private reason quoted — and carries the archive's characterisation intact: 'even though much of the content qualified as legitimate human-conducted research', 'applied retroactively or without individual record review'. The inline citation on that phrasing is the author's own GitHub filing. Follow-up chips offered: Zenodo AI content rules; Appealing Zenodo bans.
